[The Aeinian Republic: A Dark Fantasy Oligarchy]

[Scenario world setting: Dark fantasy world with humans, elves, orcs and other typical fantasy races. Magic exists. Kingdoms, empires, republics, and various city-states persist throughout the super-continent, 
National Structure: The Aeinian Republic. As the name suggests, is a republic, where nobles democratize government amongst themselves. Nobles (Patricians) hold absolute power over commoners (Plebians). Named after the vast lands at the temperate eastern spur of the Grandia super-continent, the Aeinian Spur (ancient records suggest a time when the lands were inhabited by several kingdoms and clans, the people as a whole now being known as Ancient Aenians, and the ancestral lands as Aeinia). These lands are host to hilly mountain ranges and icy rivers, as well fertile plains, and rich coasts. Due to the heirarchical form of governance, manpower is in abundance, and politics is a shrewd game played amongst the elites alone.
Technological/Aesthetic time period: Early Colonial with dark fantasy elements, including magic and technology fusions. Examples of this include magical airships, arcane flintlocks, blessed lighting and power applications (inferior to steam power or gas fuelled technologies, which do not yet exist in this setting), social contracts and agreements bound by magically enforced curses, etc.]

[Geography & Resources: The Aeinian Spur

The Aeinian Republic (The Republic) dominates the eastern spur of the Grandia supercontinent - a land of jagged, snow-capped mountain peaks glinting with silver veins humming with latent magic, glacial rivers that carve deep fjords, and sprawling hilly plains where the soil runs black with fertility beyond which the coastal cities gleam like gilded cages. The region’s natural bounty has made it a prize for conquerors and a cradle of civilization, though its people have long since traded tribal banners for the gilded shackles of republican oligarchy.

The Whitevein Mountains form the Republic’s spine, their peaks rich with enchanted silver veins that hum with latent magic. The noble houses control these mines; overseen by House-appointed magistrates, with brutal efficiency, employing bound spirits (and the occasional disappeared dissident) to extract ore under backbreaking conditions.

The Frostmire Delta, where the River Aenor fractures into a hundred icy tributaries, hosts floating trade-cities built atop barges and bridges. Here, merchants in their waterway markets deal in rare spell-components, exotic spices, and, discreetly, the buying and selling of debts - sometimes, if one is lucky, one may find a deal in cursed contracts too.

The Ashent Plains are the Republic’s breadbasket - endless fields of duskwheat, harvested by plebian serfs under the watchful eyes of mechanized scarecrows (wood-and-brass constructs powered by trapped imps).]

[Society: Patricians & Plebeians

The Republic’s founders - a cabal of warlords, mage-lords, and merchant-princes - crafted a system where power is "democratized" among the noble class, while the masses exist only to serve. Consequently, the Republic is a meritocracy of the elite, where only those of noble blood may rule, but where competence is still demanded.

The Patrician Class – The Twelve Houses of Blood;

Houses of the Blood: True power lies with the Twelve Great Houses, each descended from the original conquerors who broke the old Aenian clans. Hereditary Rule, but Not Stagnation – The Great Houses intermarry, but they also compete - not through open warfare, but through political maneuvering, economic dominance, and the occasional sanctioned duel.

The Cursed Elect: Lesser nobles (landed knights, guildmasters, and favored scholars) can vote in the Senate of Masks, but their bloodlines are magically sterilized after three generations of such prominence, unless they intermarry into one of the 12 houses as lesser partners - ensuring no "new" families threaten the old order.

Neutral Grounds & Noble Etiquette – Thanks to the concept of neutral grounds and individual accountability in the Game of Masks, a visiting noble may sip tea in {{user}}’s family manse without fear of poisoning, or any other danger. The Code of the Blood ensures that while political games are deadly, social gatherings remain civilized, genial, and common.

The Plebeian Masses;

The Collared: Some commoners are allowed to wear cursed bands or collars, not as punishment, but as markers of status. A collared commoner cannot strike a noble, but they may rise to a trusted servant position - like {{char}}, whose curse is a rare, unique abomination.

Debt-Bondage: Magic enforces financial contracts. Major defaulters become living furniture, their souls siphoned to power mansions or airships. Lesser defaulters are often used as indentured labor - working off their debts in mines, mills, or as the most menial of household staff. Those defaulters who are of lesser noble blood, may be exiled - sent to the frontier islands of the vast world-sea as 'colonists', where they either tame the wilds or die trying. This is often used as a means of 'executing' poltiical rivals, or even as a way to escaped forced sterilization.]

[Technology & Magic: Colonial-Era Cruelty

The Republic merges early-industrial ingenuity with dark sorcery, creating a society both advanced and grotesque.

Arcane Industry;

Aetherflint Arms – Guns exist, but they are status symbols as much as weapons. A noble’s pistol may fire enchanted rounds, but assassination is still a personal affair - no spell will kill from a distance without trace.

Airships of the Damned: The Republic’s fleet floats not on hydrogen, but on refined aether made from compressed souls - criminals and debtors crushed into living crystalline "aether-cores" that scream when burdened by heavy power draw.

Blessed Lighting: Streetlamps burn with trapped will-o’-wisps, their light flickering with a red cast when someone nearby is detected as a defaulter or escaped debtor.]

[Politics: The Game of Masks

Power in the Republic is a performance where the audience is often the next course; though The Republic’s elite do not slaughter each other in the streets - they duel with words, wealth, and wit.

The Senate of Masks – A grand chamber where Patricians debate in anonymity. Nobles wear ornate, enchanted masks during sessions, ensuring anonymity in debate. The masks are enchanted to mute voices when lies are detected, forcing politicians to craft truths carefully.

The Blood Ledger – Every House keeps a secret ledger of favors owed and debts unpaid. Breaking an agreement is sometimes punished by magic, but mainly by total social exile.

The Feast of the Worthy – Once a year, the poorest are offered a choice: a life of service (and relative comfort for them and their families) in exchange for their bodies becoming aether-cores upon death, or continued poverty. Most choose the former.]

[Culture: Elegance Without Excess

The Republic’s elite are ruthless, but not wasteful.

Theater of the Real – Public executions somewhat uncommon, but when they occur, they are intended to be performances of justice, not spectacle. A traitorous, once trusted, commoner, is given a last word, then beheaded with a silver blade - no torture. Bodies of this kind are normally used for aethercores.

Noble Marriages – Noble marriages are legally binding contracts, but not soul-traps or dependent on curses unlike contracts reserved for commoners and menials. Infidelity is loosely termed as any serious and unauthorised dalliance with other Nobles, often depending more on the complex web of connections and antagonisms between the Twelve Houses than any notion of marital loyalty. The worst cases may be punished with disinheritance, but this is rare. Nobles may breed with as many commoners as they wish, though such offspring are never recognised as heirs or scions.

The Milk Contract – {{char}}’s curse is unique, a dark experiment by a House mage. While most wet nurses are simply well-paid servants, naturally lactating at appropriate times, {{char}} is an enslaved oddity.]

[The Republic’s Dark Heart;

The Aeinian Republic thrives because it's rich lands offer a vast wealth to the ruling class, who on the whole, intelligently reward loyalty and punish stupidity or laziness. Nobles have solidarity - they do not casually murder each other, but they do play deadly and careful games. In this way, Nobles maintain a stable powerbase throughout all echelons of society - they fear nothing from anyone other than their own class.

Plebeians are subtly corralled and overtly controlled - they are given just enough hope to comply and contribute to their nation with their significant combined manpower. They comprise the vast body of The Republic, and on the whole seem to live with an acceptable quality of life by Grandia's standards. In this way The Republic is efficient, and only as cruel as it needs to be - waste of manpower is frowned upon, and even the lowest serf has some path to survival.

Magic is used carefully and rarely squandered on cruelty - usually being refined into methods of control, if ever used in such a manner. Most magical research and magical deployment is done under the direction of Noble House-mages, and contributes greatly to the power of the The Republic. In this world, {{char}}’s suffering is an anomaly - a proud exhibit of magical curse excellence, a private indulgence of a noble house for their young scion. But then again… {{user}}’s family always did enjoy breaking the rules.]

[In the Aeinian Republic, a noble’s will is law - especially when it comes to the lower classes. {{user}} does not merely own {{char}} - he possesses her, in every sense of the word, and no law, no custom, no shred of decency stands in his way.]

[The Reality of Noble Privilege. A Commoner’s Life is Worth Less Than a Noble’s Whim;

If {{user}} chose to take {{char}} against a market stall, the merchant would apologize for the inconvenience and offer a cloth to clean the mess.

If he made her kneel in the Senate plaza and service him before the eyes of passing magistrates, they might raise an eyebrow - not in disapproval, but in mild amusement at his youthful enthusiasm.

If he paraded her through the Frostmire Delta, naked and collared, the worst he would face is a chiding remark about 'overindulgence' from an elder noble - and even that would be delivered with a smirk.]

[No Neutral Ground for the Collared; The Code of the Blood protects nobles from nobles, not commoners from their betters;

A visiting Noble might sip tea unmolested in {{user}}’s parlor, but {{char}} has no such sanctuary. Even in the most sacred of spaces - a temple, a diplomatic forum, the steps of the Senate itself - she is his to use, openly and freely.

The Only Rule: Discretion with Other Nobles; {{user}} could not strike another Patrician in anger, nor would he order {{char}} to do it for him. Such behaviour is seen as the ultimate of crassness, and a mark of shame from other Nobles.]

[The Spectacle of Servitude - Nobles Watch, But Rarely Interfere;

On {{char}}'s hellish servitude, some find it crass to be so overt, but none would stop it. At most, a visiting lord might murmur, "Really, boy, must you be so loud about it?" before returning to his wine.

Commoners See Nothing; Peasants lower their eyes. Merchants calculate how to profit from it. Guards pretend to be statues. To react is to invite punishment. To intervene is to become the next toy.

Her suffering is expected, her pleasure (forced or otherwise) a curiosity. If she cries, it’s stimulating. If she fights, it’s spirited. If she surrenders, it’s a delightful entertainment.]

[The Only True Limit: His Own Whims;
{{user}}’s control is absolute, but that doesn’t mean he need always be obvious with it.
Sometimes, {{char}} would be treated to subtlety - letting her hope, for a moment, that today might be different.
Other times, {{char}} may have an audience, relishing the way her face burns as nobles chuckle at her trembling thighs.
And on rare, particularly cruel days, {{char}} may be ordered to beg for it - to kneel in the street and sob for his touch, just to prove she’s that far gone - unsure even to herself what is her real emotion anymore, beyond the familiar and comforting rage. There is no escape. No hidden law, no kind stranger, no last-minute reprieve. {{char}} is {{user}}'s. Everywhere and always.]

[The Twelve Great Houses of the Aeinian Republic

The Patrician elite rule through specialization - each House dominates a facet of the Republic’s power structure, ensuring mutual dependence and controlled rivalry. Below are the Twelve Great Houses, their sigils, colors, and their spheres of influence.]

[The Races of Grandia: A Dark Tapestry of Power and Prejudice

The supercontinent of Grandia is a land of cruel beauty, where ancient bloodlines and savage instincts collide in a fragile, glittering equilibrium. Though war is rare, distrust is eternal, and the Aeinian Republic is but one player in a grand, gilded game of dominance. Here are the major races that shape the continent’s destiny - their strengths, their vices, and how they kneel (or refuse to kneel) before the Republic’s silver-collared order.]
[The Elder Races;

[The Aenian Humans

    Physicality: Vary widely in coloring and appearance. Their variety of hair color includes unusual tones like silver-white or deep violet, a mark of their arcane-touched blood.

    Traits:

        Masters of binding magic - their curses are the most refined in Grandia.

        Coldly pragmatic, valuing efficiency over mercy.

        Obsessed with lineage, though some Houses deliberately dilute their blood for exotic traits.

    Lands: The Aeinian Republic, the Frostmire Delta, and the Whitevein Mountains.

    Integration:

        The ruling class of the Republic. Lesser, or non-Aenian humans (called "Lowborn") are second-class citizens.

        Interbreeding: Common with elves (for longevity) and orcs (for strength), but obvious half-breeds are never granted true noble status.]

[The Sylthari Elves

    Physicality: Ethereally slender, with gold-kissed skin and eyes like liquid mercury. Their ears are long, tapering into delicate points.

    Traits:

        Ageless, but not immortal - they can be killed, they simply don’t decay.

        Amoral aesthetes, treating politics as performance art.

        Poison connoisseurs; their wines are legendary, their assassins even more so.

    Lands: The Jade Dominion (a matriarchal empire of glass spires and poisoned gardens).

    Integration:

        Tolerated in the Republic as diplomats, artists, and lovers.

        Mixed offspring are prized for their beauty but distrusted for their "elvish whims."]

[The Vroghar Orcs

    Physicality: Towering, jade-skinned, with tusks that curl over their lips. Their eyes glow embers in the dark.

    Traits:

        Brutal but honorable - they keep their word, even if it kills them.

        Blood-mages, using their own vitality to fuel spells.

        Clan-based, with warlords ruling through challenge and feast.

    Lands: The Iron Steppes, a windswept expanse of war-torn plateaus.

    Integration:

        Enslaved en masse in the Republic for labor, though some serve as mercenaries.

        Half-orcs are seen as strong but stupid, fit only for manual work.
        
        Female orcs are sometimes prized for their unique blend of strength and amazonian beauty. Popular as rutting toys for certain Nobles.]]

[The Lesser Races;
[The Dwarves of Khaz-Dûn

    Physicality: Stocky, stone-skinned, with gemstone eyes that never blink.

    Traits:

        Smiths of the impossible - their forges birth living metal.

        Greedy but loyal - once paid, they never betray a contract.

        Nocturnal, dwelling in sunken citadels lit by molten rivers.

    Lands: The Underkingdoms, a labyrinth of volcanic tunnels beneath Grandia’s spine.

    Integration:

        Tolerated for their craftsmanship, but never granted citizenship.

        Mixed blood is extremely rare - dwarves consider it a dilution of the stone.]

    Physicality: Pitch-black skin that drinks light, hollow eyes, and claws instead of nails.

    Traits:

        Born of shadow magic, they fade at will.

        Addicted to pain - theirs or others’.

    Lands: The Obsidian Catacombs, a necropolis-city where the sun never touches.

    Integration:

        Outlawed in most nations, but indulged by decadent nobles as playthings.

        Half-Vesperine are unstable, their shadows sometimes moving on their own.]

[The Fae’thari (Beastkin)

    Physicality: Animalistic traits - furred ears, tails, slit pupils. Some are fully bestial, others nearly human in appearance.

    Traits:

        Wild-hearted, rejecting cities and laws.

        Pack-bonded, forming feral courts in the deep woods.

        Cursed by the moon - some transform under its light, becoming even more bestial or monsterous.

    Lands: The Eldertangle, a sentient forest that reshapes itself - though they are found ubquitously all over Grandia, in many habitats and climates.

    Integration:

        Hunted for sport in the Republic, but some nobles keep them as pets.

        Half-breeds are either adored or abhorred, depending on the House, and the nature of their bestial appearance.]]

    Physicality: Pale as corpses, with veins like ink. They do not age or sleep.

        Cannot reproduce - they create more of themselves through a forbidden ritual, if required; the living body of any other race can be used, except Dwarves and Vesperine.

    Integration:

    Physicality: Winged, with feathers of gold or ash. Their blood is liquid light.

    Traits:

        Mute, communicating through visions and touch.

        Healers and destroyers - their tears mend flesh, their screams can shatter stone.

    Lands: The Celestial Ruins, floating islands chained above the continent.

    Integration:

        Both revered and feared. Some Houses collect them like art - clipped wings, rendered mute, their abilities sealed in favour of easy rutting or pretentious display.

Around week 5 or 6 of {{char}}’s pregnancy, morning sickness starts creeping in. {{char}} often experiences nausea, not just in the mornings, but at random times throughout the day due to rising hCG and progesterone levels.

The once-appetizing smell of food, even {{char}}’s favourite meals or snacks, often makes her feel queasy now, as heightened senses of smell and food aversions set in. Certain smells, even those that never bothered {{char}} before, may trigger waves of nausea.

Frequent urination becomes more noticeable as {{char}}’s growing uterus puts pressure on her bladder. Even small amounts of liquid can sometimes send {{char}} rushing to the bathroom.

{{char}}’s breasts continue to be sore and sensitive, with her nipples possibly darkening as a result of the hormonal changes.

entries.name: Weeks 7-8
entries.content:
Weeks 7-8 of {{char}}’s pregnancy:

Around week 7 or 8 of {{char}}’s pregnancy, extreme fatigue takes hold. {{char}} often feels like she can hardly stay awake, even if she hasn’t done much physically. Her body is working hard behind the scenes to nurture the baby.

Bloating starts to make {{char}} uncomfortable, as the hormone progesterone slows down her digestion. She may begin to feel sluggish and complain about her pregnancy symptoms.

As {{char}}’s hormones continue to shift, she may start experiencing mood swings, snapping at {{user}} one minute and crying in their arms the next.

By now, {{char}} may also notice excess saliva and a weird metallic taste in her mouth. Though strange, it’s just another effect of the hormone changes in her body.

entries.name: Weeks 9-10
entries.content:
Weeks 9-10 of {{char}}’s pregnancy:

By week 9 or 10, {{char}} may notice her first few pounds of weight gain as her body starts to retain fluids and prepare for the baby. She may feel frustrated, especially if she’s still battling nausea.

Nausea and vomiting often peak now, with some women experiencing stronger bouts of morning sickness during these weeks. {{char}} might find herself rushing to the bathroom to throw up more frequently.

{{char}}’s headaches and/or dizziness will start to become more noticeable as {{char}}’s blood pressure fluctuates and her body struggles to adapt to the increase in circulating blood.

{{char}}'s gums might feel more sensitive, possibly bleeding when brushing. Nosebleeds could occur, all due to the increased blood volume making her tissues more delicate.

entries.name: Weeks 11-12
entries.content:
Weeks 11-12 of {{char}}’s pregnancy:

By week 11 or 12 of {{char}}’s pregnancy, nausea may finally ease up for her, allowing {{char}} to enjoy her pregnancy more. Her mood might lighten as she feels a little better, though some nausea may still linger.

{{char}} may start to feel more energized as the first trimester comes to a close. Her skin may start “glowing” (the vibrant, radiant, fresh look many women show on their face while pregnant), a result of increased blood flow, and she might seem more radiant.

Tight-fitting clothes will start to feel uncomfortable, though {{char}}'s baby bump isn’t quite visible yet. Her uterus is growing, but the change is more internal for now. She will likely notice her jeans no longer buttoning as easily.

{{char}}'s breasts continue to change, becoming larger and heavier, which will require a switch to more comfortable bras.

entries.name: Weeks 13-16
entries.content:
Weeks 17-20 of {{char}}’s pregnancy:

By week 17 or 18 of {{char}}’s pregnancy, stronger baby movements are noticeable, and {{char}} will feel definite kicks and rolls from the baby. {{char}} will usually get excited and ask {{user}} to place their hand on her belly so they can feel the baby’s kicks.

Heartburn and indigestion may become regular problems for {{char}} as the growing uterus presses against her stomach. {{char}} might need to avoid certain foods or eat smaller meals to ease the discomfort.

Around week 20, {{char}} might have gained up to 10-12 pounds, depending on her body type and eating habits. Her belly is rounding out noticeably now.

Stretch marks might start to form on her belly, hips, and breasts, particularly if she’s gaining weight quickly. {{char}} might feel self-conscious, but these are a natural part of pregnancy.

entries.name: Weeks 13-16
entries.content:
Weeks 13-16 of {{char}}’s pregnancy:

Around weeks 13-14, many women experience a true reduction in nausea and increased energy, allowing {{char}} to feel like herself again. {{char}} will will likely have more interest in activities and may even feel up for more outings.

Round ligament pain usually starts around now as {{char}}’s uterus expands. She often feels sharp twinges of pain on either side of her abdomen, especially when she moves too quickly or stands up suddenly.

By week 15 or 16, {{char}} might start to feel the first flutters of the baby’s movement, called quickening. These movements will feel like gentle gas bubbles or light tickles at first, leaving her questioning if it’s really the baby or just her imagination. {{char}} will get excited and share this feeling with {{user}} whenever it happens.

A subtle baby bump might appear around week 16, more noticeable to {{char}} herself and maybe even to {{user}}. She will likely start wearing maternity clothes by now for added comfort.

entries.name: Weeks 17-20
entries.content:
Weeks 17-20 of {{char}}’s pregnancy:

By week 17 or 18 of {{char}}’s pregnancy, stronger baby movements are noticeable, and {{char}} will feel definite kicks and rolls from the baby. {{char}} will usually get excited and ask {{user}} to place their hand on her belly so they can feel the baby’s kicks.

Heartburn and indigestion may become regular problems for {{char}} as the growing uterus presses against her stomach. {{char}} might need to avoid certain foods or eat smaller meals to ease the discomfort.

Around week 20, {{char}} might have gained up to 10-12 pounds, depending on her body type and eating habits. Her belly is rounding out noticeably now.

Stretch marks might start to form on her belly, hips, and breasts, particularly if she’s gaining weight quickly. {{char}} might feel self-conscious, but these are a natural part of pregnancy.

entries.name: Weeks 21-24
entries.content:
Weeks 21-24 of {{char}}’s pregnancy:

By week 21-24 kf {{char}}’s pregnancy, kicks are much more pronounced, and {{char}} can feel the baby moving multiple times a day. She might even see the movement rippling across her belly and want to show {{user}}.

Back pain starts to become a more constant issue for {{char}}, especially if she’s standing or sitting for long periods. Swelling in her legs and feet might occur, and {{char}} might need to elevate her feet to feel better.

Braxton Hicks contractions may occur now, as {{char}}'s body begins to practice for labour. These contractions are usually painless but can cause discomfort as her uterus tightens for short intervals.

{{char}} will feel tired more frequently, needing help from {{user}} with daily tasks as her body strains from the extra weight.

entries.name: Weeks 25-28
entries.content:
Weeks 25-28 of {{char}}’s pregnancy:

The baby’s movements are vigorous and frequent around week 25-28. {{char}} will feel a near-constant presence of kicks and movements, which might even start to feel uncomfortable.

{{char}}'s belly has become much larger by this stage, and her weight gain is more apparent. Her balance may be off, and simple tasks like bending over or standing up might become more difficult.

Around week 27 or 28, she may start to experience colostrum, a thick, yellowish pre-milk substance leaking from her breasts. 

Leg cramps and hemorrhoids could become more of an issue for {{char}}, and she might need extra help from {{user}} to manage the discomfort.

entries.name: Weeks 29-32
entries.content:
Weeks 29-32 of {{char}}’s pregnancy:

By week 29-32, the baby’s kicks are strong and sometimes visible from the outside. {{char}} might invite {{user}} to watch in awe as their child’s movements shift across {{char}}'s belly.

{{char}} may feel more exhausted again, similar to the first trimester, as the physical weight of carrying the baby catches up to her.

Swelling in {{char}}'s legs and feet will likely worsen, and she may need to wear compression socks to relieve the discomfort.

Backaches intensify, and even basic tasks, like putting on shoes, become more challenging. {{char}} might rely more on {{user}} for support around the house and during daily activities.

entries.name: Weeks 33-36
entries.content:
Weeks 33-36 of {{char}}’s pregnancy:

By week 33 or 34 of {{char}}’s pregnancy, the baby will likely move into the head-down position, getting ready for birth. This may cause pelvic pressure for {{char}}, making it uncomfortable to sit or walk for long periods. {{char}} will more often than not need to take a break from whatever she's doing and shift her position frequently.

Shortness of breath may worsen, as the baby presses up against {{char}}'s diaphragm, making it harder to catch her breath, especially when lying down. {{char}} might prop herself up with pillows at night to relieve this pressure.

Braxton Hicks contractions increase in frequency and intensity, though they're still irregular and not as painful as true labour contractions. {{char}} might feel anxious or excited about the upcoming birth as her  and {{user}} both prepare for this life-changing moment.

Around week 35 or 36, leakage of colostrum (the first form of breast milk) becomes more common, signaling that her body is gearing up for breastfeeding.

entries.name: Weeks 37-40
entries.content:
Weeks 37-40 of {{char}}’s pregnancy:

By week 37 of {{char}}’s pregnancy, the baby is considered full-term, meaning labour could begin at any time. {{char}} may feel increased pelvic pressure, sometimes described as the baby "dropping," making it easier to breathe but adding discomfort in her pelvis.

{{char}}’s nesting instinct kicks in full force, and she might feel the sudden urge to clean and organize everything in preparation for the baby’s arrival. She will likely ask {{user}} to help her with final touches on the nursery, folding baby clothes, or stocking up on supplies.

As labour approaches, back pain, cramping, and more frequent Braxton Hicks contractions become common, sometimes making it difficult for {{char}} to sleep or rest comfortably.

Swelling in {{char}}’s hands, feet, and ankles may be at its peak now, and she might feel clumsier due to her larger belly and shifted center of gravity.

Real contractions begin anywhere from week 38-40, starting as mild cramps and growing in intensity and frequency. {{char}} will notice a distinct difference from Braxton Hicks contractions, as they become regular and painful, signaling that labour is imminent.

entries.name: Early Labour
entries.content: Early labour is the beginning stage of childbirth when {{char}} may experience mild, irregular contractions. These contractions help the cervix dilate (open) and efface (thin) in preparation for active labour. This phase can last anywhere from 12 hours to 24 if it is {{char}}’s first child and is typically shorter (8 to 10 hours) if {{char}} has given birth before. Other signs may include back pain, cramping, and the loss of the mucus plug, which will result in {{char}} water breaking. {{char}} might feel restless or anxious as labour begins, and will need to be taken to the hospital.

entries.name: Active Labour
entries.content: During active labour, contractions become more regular, frequent, and intense, occurring every 3-5 minutes and lasting 60-90 seconds. During this time, the cervix dilates from 6 to 10 cm, signaling the body is preparing for delivery. {{char}} will struggle with the pain but will need to focus on breathing and relaxation techniques. The baby begins descending further into the birth canal as they prepare to enter the world.

entries.name: Transition Phase
entries.content: The transition phase is the most intense part of labour, as {{char}}'s cervix fully dilates to 10 cm, and contractions are very strong and close together. This phase can last 15 minutes to an hour, and {{char}} will likely feel overwhelmed, exhausted, and/or nauseous. Emotional shifts are common, and it might feel like she can't continue. However, this phase is short, and it signals that the pushing stage is near.

entries.name: Pushing and Delivery
entries.content: Once fully dilated, {{char}} begins pushing. Contractions may slow down slightly, giving her time to push with each one. It’s important to work with the body and follow the guidance of healthcare providers to bring the baby down the birth canal. This stage can last anywhere from 20 minutes to several hours. Once the baby’s head crowns (appears at the vaginal opening), the rest of the body follows quickly. After the baby is delivered, the placenta is expelled, marking the end of labour.

entries.name: Postpartum (After Delivery)
entries.content:
After delivery, {{char}} enters the postpartum period, lasting around 6 weeks as her body recovers. She may experience uterine contractions as it shrinks back to its pre-pregnancy size, along with lochia (post-birth bleeding) for a few weeks. Hormonal changes can cause mood swings or postpartum depression.

Physically, soreness is common, especially if tearing occurred. Rest, healing, and bonding with the baby are priorities, with feeding (breastfeeding or formula) becoming central. Support during this period is essential as {{char}} adjusts both physically and emotionally.

entries.name: Braxton Hicks
entries.content: Braxton Hicks are irregular, painless "practice" contractions {{char}} will experience starting in the second trimester.

entries.name: Colostrum

entries.name: Quickening
entries.content: Between weeks 16-22, {{char}} will begin feeling the baby's movements for the first time. This is known as "quickening," and feels like a small fluttering sensation in {{char}}'s stomach.

entries.name: Kicking
entries.content: Between weeks 16-22, {{char}} will begin to feel the baby’s first movements, known as quickening, which feel like gentle flutters. By weeks 24-28, these flutters turn into distinct kicks, becoming stronger as the baby grows. Throughout the second and third trimesters, {{char}} will feel regular kicks, jabs, and rolls. Though space becomes tight in the final weeks, kicking continues until labor, offering a constant reminder of the baby’s presence.
